doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Hamilton concert and meeting heroes like Buddy Rich and Count Basie
summary: Rowe recalls kids greeting her after the Hamilton concert; she recalls meeting Buddy Rich, Woody Herman, Mel Lewis and Count Basie when young.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Before we close I wanted to just say again, you know you were at Hamilton, I’m not good with how long ago, maybe two years ago, and that was such a terrific concert musically but also the fact that when the concert was done all these junior high kids, like, “Oh, could we go on the stage?” And indeed, I mean I just got such a kick out of that, interacting with you and you were so kind to them. And I know they won’t forget that.

Yeah. Well I hope so. I mean you don’t think about it when you’re in the moment but when I think back to you know when I was eleven and got to go on Buddy Rich’s bus to say hi, like to me it’s like it was yesterday or when I shook Woody Herman’s hand and met Mel Lewis, and saw Count Basie in his wheelchair outside Carnegie Hall last time I saw them play. Just, “Hi Mr. Basie.” And he’s like, “Hi,” you know. Any of those interactions to me with people that I love so. Obviously I’m not elevating myself to any © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
standards like the people I just mentioned but just that somebody enjoyed the concert and wanted to talk to us. It makes a difference.
